Main.sentence: Barack Hussein Obama II [a] (born August 4, 1961) is an American politician who served as the 44th ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ from 2009 to 2017. A member of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ , he was the first ___E:African American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American)___ president.

Obama previously served as a ___E:U.S. senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._senator)___ representing Illinois from 2005 to 2008 and as an ___E:Illinois state senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_state_senator)___ from 1997 to 2004.

Born in ___E:Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu)___ , Hawaii, Obama graduated from ___E:Columbia University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University)___ in 1983 with a ___E:Bachelor of Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ degree in political science and later worked as a ___E:community organizer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_organizer)___ in ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ .
In 1988, Obama enrolled in ___E:Harvard Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_School)___ , where he was the first black president of the Harvard Law Review .

He became a civil rights attorney and an academic, teaching ___E:constitutional law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_law)___ at the ___E:University of Chicago Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Law_School)___ from 1992 to 2004. In 1996, Obama was elected to ___E:represent the 13th district in the Illinois Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Senate_career_of_Barack_Obama)___ , a position he held until 2004, when he ___E:successfully ran for the U.S. Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_Senate_election_in_Illinois)___ .

In the ___E:2008 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election)___ , after ___E:a close primary campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries)___ against ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ , he was nominated by the Democratic Party for president.

Obama selected ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ as his running mate and defeated ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ nominee ___E:John McCain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain)___ and his running mate ___E:Sarah Palin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Palin)___ .
Obama was awarded the ___E:2009 Nobel Peace Prize U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Nobel_Peace_Prize)___ for efforts in international diplomacy, a decision which drew both criticism and praise.

During his first term, his administration responded to the ___E:2008 financial crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis)___ with measures including the ___E:American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Recovery_and_Reinvestment_Act_of_2009)___ , a major stimulus package to guide the economy in recovering from the ___E:Great Recession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession)___ ; a partial extension of the ___E:Bush tax cuts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bush_tax_cuts)___ ; ___E:legislation to reform health care U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care_reforms_proposed_during_the_Obama_administration)___ ; and the ___E:Dodd–Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodd%E2%80%93Frank_Wall_Street_Reform_and_Consumer_Protection_Act)___ , a major financial regulation reform bill. Obama also appointed ___E:Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States)___ justices ___E:Sonia Sotomayor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonia_Sotomayor)___ and ___E:Elena Kagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elena_Kagan)___ , the former being the first ___E:Hispanic American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_American)___ on the Supreme Court.

He oversaw the end of the ___E:Iraq War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War)___ and ordered ___E:Operation Neptune Spear U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Neptune_Spear)___ , the raid that killed ___E:Osama bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden)___ , who was responsible for the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ .

Obama downplayed Bush's ___E:counterinsurgency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counterinsurgency)___ model, expanding ___E:air strikes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_strikes)___ and making extensive use of special forces, while encouraging greater reliance on host-government militaries.

He also ordered the ___E:2011 military intervention in Libya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_military_intervention_in_Libya)___ to implement ___E:United Nations Security Council Resolution 1973 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_1973)___ , contributing to the overthrow of ___E:Muammar Gaddafi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muammar_Gaddafi)___ .

Obama defeated Republican opponent ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ and his running mate ___E:Paul Ryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Ryan_(politician))___ in the ___E:2012 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

In his second term, Obama advocated for ___E:gun control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_politics_in_the_United_States)___ in the wake of the ___E:Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandy_Hook_Elementary_School_shooting)___ , took steps to ___E:combat climate change U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combat_climate_change)___ , signing the ___E:Paris Agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Agreement)___ , a major international climate agreement, and an ___E:executive order U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_order)___ to limit ___E:carbon emissions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_emission)___ .

Obama also presided over the implementation of the ___E:Affordable Care Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act)___ and other legislation passed in his first term. He initiated ___E:sanctions against Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_sanctions_during_the_Ukrainian_crisis)___ following the ___E:invasion in Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_military_intervention_in_Ukraine_(2014%E2%80%93present))___ and again after ___E:Russian interference in the 2016 U.S. elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_interference_in_the_2016_U.S._elections)___ , ordered ___E:military intervention in Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American-led_intervention_in_Iraq_(2014%E2%80%93present))___ in response to gains made by ___E:ISIL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISIL)___ following the 2011 withdrawal from Iraq, negotiated the ___E:Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Comprehensive_Plan_of_Action)___ (a nuclear agreement with Iran), and ___E:normalized relations with Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_thaw)___ .

The number of ___E:American soldiers in Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%932021))___ decreased during Obama's second term, though U.S. soldiers remained in the country throughout the remainder of his presidency.

Obama promoted inclusion for ___E:LGBT Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_Americans)___ , becoming the first sitting U.S. president to publicly support ___E:same-sex marriage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_the_United_States)___ .
Obama left office in 2017 with high approval ratings both within the United States and among foreign advisories.

He continues to reside in Washington, D.C., and remains politically active, campaigning for candidates in various American elections, including in Biden's ___E:successful presidential bid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_2020_presidential_campaign)___ in the ___E:2020 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

Outside of politics, ___E:Obama has published three books U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bibliography_of_Barack_Obama)___ : Dreams from My Father (1995) , The Audacity of Hope (2006), and A Promised Land (2020). ___E:His presidential library U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Presidential_Center)___ began construction in the ___E:South Side of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side_of_Chicago)___ in 2021. Historians and political scientists rank Obama among the upper tier in ___E:historical rankings of U.S. presidents U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States#Scholar_survey_summary)___ .

Barack Obama was born on August 4, 1961,  at ___E:Kapiolani Medical Center for Women and Children U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapiolani_Medical_Center_for_Women_and_Children)___ in ___E:Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu)___ , Hawaii.
He is the only president born outside the ___E:contiguous 48 states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contiguous_United_States)___ .
He was born to an 18-year-old American mother and a 27-year-old Kenyan father.

His mother, ___E:Ann Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Dunham)___ (1942–1995), was born in ___E:Wichita, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas)___ , and was of English, Welsh, German, Swiss, and Irish descent.

In 2007 it was discovered her great-great-grandfather Falmouth Kearney emigrated from the village of ___E:Moneygall, Ireland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moneygall)___ to the U.S. in 1850.  In July 2012, ___E:Ancestry.com U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancestry.com)___ found a strong likelihood that Dunham was descended from ___E:John Punch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Punch_(slave))___ , an enslaved African man who lived in the ___E:Colony of Virginia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_Virginia)___ during the seventeenth century.
Obama has described the ancestors of his grandparents as ___E:Scotch-Irish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotch-Irish_Americans)___ mostly.

Obama's father, ___E:Barack Obama Sr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.)___ (1934–1982),  was a married    ___E:Luo Kenyan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_people_of_Kenya_and_Tanzania)___ from ___E:Nyang'oma Kogelo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang%27oma_Kogelo)___ .
His last name, Obama, was derived from his Luo descent.

Obama's parents met in 1960 in a Russian language class at the ___E:University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_at_M%C4%81noa)___ , where his father was a foreign student on a scholarship.
The couple married in ___E:Wailuku, Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wailuku,_Hawaii)___ , on February 2, 1961, six months before Obama was born.

In late August 1961, a few weeks after he was born, Barack and his mother moved to the ___E:University of Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Washington)___ in ___E:Seattle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle)___ , where they lived for a year. During that time, Barack's father completed his undergraduate degree in economics in Hawaii, graduating in June 1962. He left to attend graduate school on a scholarship at ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ , where he earned a ___E:Master of Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Arts)___ in economics.

Obama's parents divorced in March 1964.  Obama Sr. returned to ___E:Kenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya)___ in 1964, where he married for a third time and worked for the Kenyan government as the senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance.  [page needed] He visited his son in Hawaii only once, at Christmas 1971,  before he was killed in an automobile accident in 1982, when Obama was 21 years old.  Recalling his early childhood, Obama said: "That my father looked nothing like the people around me—that he was black as pitch, my mother white as milk—barely registered in my mind."  He described his struggles as a young adult to reconcile social perceptions of his multiracial heritage.

In 1963, Dunham met ___E:Lolo Soetoro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lolo_Soetoro)___ at the ___E:University of Hawaiʻi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi)___ ; he was an Indonesian ___E:East–West Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East%E2%80%93West_Center)___ graduate student in geography.

The couple married on ___E:Molokai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molokai)___ on March 15, 1965.  After two one-year extensions of his ___E:J-1 visa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J-1_visa)___ , Lolo returned to Indonesia in 1966. His wife and stepson followed sixteen months later in 1967. The family initially lived in the Menteng Dalam neighborhood in the ___E:Tebet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tebet,_South_Jakarta)___ district of ___E:South Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Jakarta)___ .

From 1970, they lived in a wealthier neighborhood in the ___E:Menteng U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menteng)___ district of ___E:Central Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Jakarta)___ .
When he was six years old, Obama and his mother had moved to Indonesia to join his stepfather.

From age six to ten, he was registered in school as "Barry"  and attended local ___E:Indonesian-language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_Language)___ schools: Sekolah Dasar Katolik Santo Fransiskus Asisi (St. Francis of Assisi Catholic Elementary School) for two years and ___E:Sekolah Dasar Negeri Menteng 01 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Elementary_School_Menteng_01)___ (State Elementary School Menteng 01) for one and a half years, supplemented by English-language ___E:Calvert School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvert_School)___ homeschooling by his mother.

As a result of his four years in ___E:Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta)___ , he was able to speak ___E:Indonesian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_language)___ fluently as a child.
During his time in Indonesia, Obama's stepfather taught him to be resilient and gave him "a pretty hardheaded assessment of how the world works".

In 1971, Obama returned to Honolulu to live with his maternal grandparents, ___E:Madelyn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelyn_Dunham)___ and ___E:Stanley Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham)___ .

He attended ___E:Punahou School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punahou_School)___ —a private ___E:college preparatory school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University-preparatory_school)___ —with the aid of a scholarship from fifth grade until he graduated from high school in 1979.  In high school, Obama continued to use the nickname "Barry" which he kept until making a visit to Kenya in 1980.  Obama lived with his mother and half-sister, ___E:Maya Soetoro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maya_Soetoro-Ng)___ , in Hawaii for three years from 1972 to 1975 while his mother was a graduate student in ___E:anthropology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropology)___ at the University of Hawaii.

Obama chose to stay in Hawaii when his mother and half-sister returned to Indonesia in 1975, so his mother could begin anthropology field work.  His mother spent most of the next two decades in Indonesia, divorcing Lolo Soetoro in 1980 and earning a PhD degree in 1992, before dying in 1995 in Hawaii following unsuccessful treatment for ___E:ovarian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_cancer)___ and ___E:uterine cancer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterine_cancer)___ .

Of his years in Honolulu, Obama wrote: "The opportunity that Hawaii offered — to experience a variety of cultures in a climate of mutual respect — became an integral part of my world view, and a basis for the values that I hold most dear."  Obama has also written and talked about using ___E:alcohol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_(drug))___ , ___E:marijuana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marijuana)___ , and ___E:cocaine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine)___ during his teenage years to "push questions of who I was out of my mind".
Obama was also a member of the "Choom Gang" (the slang term for smoking marijuana), a self-named group of friends who spent time together and smoked marijuana.
College and research jobs
After graduating from high school in 1979, Obama moved to Los Angeles to attend ___E:Occidental College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occidental_College)___ on a full scholarship.

In February 1981, Obama made his first public speech, calling for Occidental to participate in the ___E:disinvestment from South Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disinvestment_from_South_Africa)___ in response to that nation's policy of ___E:apartheid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid)___ .

In mid-1981, Obama traveled to Indonesia to visit his mother and half-sister Maya and visited the families of college friends in ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan)___ for three weeks.

Later in 1981, he ___E:transferred U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_transfer)___ to ___E:Columbia University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University)___ in New York City as a ___E:junior U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_(education_year))___ , where he majored in ___E:political science U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_science)___ with a specialty in ___E:international relations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_relations)___  and in ___E:English literature U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_literature)___  and lived off-campus on West 109th Street.
He graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1983 and a 3.7 ___E:GPA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grading_(education)#United_States)___ .

After graduating, Obama worked for about a year at the ___E:Business International Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_International_Corporation)___ , where he was a financial researcher and writer,   then as a project coordinator for the ___E:New York Public Interest Research Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Public_Interest_Research_Group)___ on the ___E:City College of New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_College_of_New_York)___ campus for three months in 1985.
Community organizer and Harvard Law School

Two years after graduating from Columbia, Obama moved from New York to Chicago when he was hired as director of the ___E:Developing Communities Project U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_Communities_Project)___ , a faith-based community organization originally comprising eight Catholic parishes in ___E:Roseland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roseland,_Chicago)___ , ___E:West Pullman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pullman,_Chicago)___ , and ___E:Riverdale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale,_Chicago)___ on Chicago's ___E:South Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side,_Chicago)___ .

He worked there as a community organizer from June 1985 to May 1988.   He helped set up a job training program, a college preparatory tutoring program, and a tenants' rights organization in ___E:Altgeld Gardens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altgeld_Gardens_Homes_(Chicago,_Illinois))___ .
Obama also worked as a consultant and instructor for the ___E:Gamaliel Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamaliel_Foundation)___ , a community organizing institute.

In mid-1988, he traveled for the first time in ___E:Europe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe)___ for three weeks and then for five weeks in Kenya, where he met many of his ___E:paternal relatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jael_Obama)___ for the first time.

Despite being offered a full scholarship to ___E:Northwestern University School of Law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_University_School_of_Law)___ , Obama enrolled at ___E:Harvard Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Law_School)___ in the fall of 1988, living in nearby ___E:Somerville, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somerville,_Massachusetts)___ .

He was selected as an editor of the Harvard Law Review at the end of his first year,  president of the journal in his second year,   and research assistant to the constitutional scholar ___E:Laurence Tribe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Tribe)___ while at Harvard.

During his summers, he returned to Chicago, where he worked as a ___E:summer associate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associate_attorney#Summer_associates)___ at the law firms of ___E:Sidley Austin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidley_Austin)___ in 1989 and ___E:Hopkins & Sutter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hopkins_%26_Sutter)___ in 1990.  Obama's election as the ___E:first black president of the Harvard Law Review U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_African-American_firsts)___ gained national media attention   and led to a publishing contract and advance for a book about race relations,  which evolved into a personal memoir.
The manuscript was published in mid-1995 as Dreams from My Father .
Obama graduated from Harvard Law in 1991 with a ___E:Juris Doctor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor)___ magna cum laude .
University of Chicago Law School

In 1991, Obama accepted a two-year position as Visiting Law and Government Fellow at the ___E:University of Chicago Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Law_School)___ to work on his first book.   He then taught ___E:constitutional law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutional_law)___ at the University of Chicago Law School for twelve years, first as a lecturer from 1992 to 1996, and then as a senior lecturer from 1996 to 2004.

From April to October 1992, Obama directed Illinois's ___E:Project Vote U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Vote)___ , a ___E:voter registration campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voter_registration_campaign)___ with ten staffers and seven hundred volunteer registrars; it achieved its goal of registering 150,000 of 400,000 unregistered African Americans in the state, leading Crain's Chicago Business to name Obama to its 1993 list of "40 under Forty" powers to be.

In a 2006 interview, Obama highlighted the diversity of ___E:his extended family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_of_Barack_Obama)___ : "It's like a little mini-United Nations," he said. "I've got relatives who look like ___E:Bernie Mac U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Mac)___ , and I've got relatives who look like ___E:Margaret Thatcher U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Thatcher)___ ."  Obama has a half-sister with whom he was raised (Maya Soetoro-Ng) and seven other half-siblings from his Kenyan father's family, six of them living.
Obama's mother was survived by her Kansas-born mother, Madelyn Dunham,  until her death on November 2, 2008,  two days before his election to the presidency.

Obama also has roots in Ireland; he met with his Irish cousins in ___E:Moneygall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moneygall)___ in May 2011.  In Dreams from My Father , Obama ties his mother's family history to possible Native American ancestors and distant relatives of ___E:Jefferson Davis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Davis)___ , ___E:President of the Confederate States of America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Confederate_States_of_America)___ during the ___E:American Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War)___ .

He also shares distant ancestors in common with ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ and ___E:Dick Cheney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Cheney)___ , among others.
Obama lived with anthropologist ___E:Sheila Miyoshi Jager U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheila_Miyoshi_Jager)___ while he was a community organizer in Chicago in the 1980s.
He proposed to her twice, but both Jager and her parents turned him down.   The relationship was not made public until May 2017, several months after his presidency had ended.
In June 1989, Obama met ___E:Michelle Robinson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama)___ when he was employed at ___E:Sidley Austin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidley_Austin)___ .

Robinson was assigned for three months as Obama's adviser at the firm, and she joined him at several group social functions but declined his initial requests to date.
